title: Combinatorial Synthesis of and High-throughput Protein Release from Polymer Film and Nanoparticle Libraries
protocol: Dissolve each monomer in the appropriate solvent to a concentration of 25 mg/ml.
Load each dissolved monomer into a 10cc gas tight syringe.
Attach solvent resistant lure lock capillary tubes to the end of each syringe.
Place the syringes on the syringe pumps and lock them into position.
Set the linear actuators to the starting position.
Position the end of both capillary tubes into the starting vial/well for monomer deposition using ring stand clamps.
Initiate the LabVIEW program to pump variable volumes of each monomer into each well depending upon the desired copolymer composition.
Instruct the Z-axis actuator to lower the capillary tubes into the vial/well and then instruct each pump to dispense the desired volume.
Return the Z-actuator to its home position after dispensing.
Move the X- and Y- actuators to the position of the next vial/well for subsequent deposition.
Deposite the desired volume of monomer in each well until all wells have the correct volumes.
Transfer the multi-well or multi-vial monomer library to a pre-heated vacuum oven.
Incubate under vacuum for the duration of the condensation polymerization reaction.
Fill the syringe in the first programmable syringe pump with a solvent or a solvent containing dispersed protein.
Leave the syringe in the second syringe pump empty.
Fill tubes for nanoparticle fabrication in the adjacent sample holder with non-solvent (ratio of solvent to non-solvent is 1 to 100).
Utilize an empty multi-well plate for film fabrication instead of the tubes in the adjacent sample holder.
Deposit the solvent into all polymer vials/wells of the library using LabVIEW program (concentration = 20 mg/ml).
Incubate the deposited solvent for 1-5 minutes.
Optionally sonicate the sample for 30 seconds at 40 Hz to ensure complete polymer dissolution.
Withdraw the sample into the empty syringe and deposit it into its corresponding tube of non-solvent (nanoparticles) or empty well (films).
Place the nanoparticle or film library in a vacuum chamber for solvent and non-solvent removal.
Recover the nanoparticle library using vacuum filtration if necessary.
Modify the top 1/3 of the well wall in neighboring columns of a 96 deep-welled polypropylene plate to adjoin the wells.
Place protein-loaded films or nanoparticles only in one well of the adjoining columns (e.g., A, C, E, G).
Transfer nanoparticles to the designated sample wells (columns A, C, E, and G) carefully.
Allow the particles to settle in the sample wells.
Add PBS buffer (0.1 mM, pH 7.4) slowly to each sample well until full.
Ensure that the buffer is free-flowing between adjoining wells without transferring nanoparticles.
If necessary, use centrifugation to localize nanoparticle samples at the bottom of the designated sample wells.
Seal the release plate with a lid.
Place the sealed release plate at the desired temperature (e.g., 37 °C).
Agitate the plate for the duration of the experiment.
At incremental time points, place the release plate on a 9400 Typhoon Flatbed Fluorescent Scanner.
Scan the plate using the appropriate excitation laser and emission filters.
Quantify the fluorescence intensity of the released protein in columns B, D, F, and H.
Include protein standards of known concentrations for calculating protein quantity.
Account for fluorochrome quenching when determining protein concentration.
